points.description: Identifies the context: Plato's theory of the soul (the appetitive faculty is one of the three parts/divisions of the soul, with reason and spirit).
points.partial_credit: Half if only says it is a part of the soul without naming Plato or his theory, or is vague about it being one of three.

points.description: States that the appetitive faculty is the part dealing with desires and passions (bodily appetites/urges, e.g. hunger, thirst, sex).
points.partial_credit: Half if the description is vague or only partly right (e.g. just 'emotions' or 'wants').

rubric.notes: Full marks: the answer links the appetitive faculty to Plato's theory of the soul (one of its parts) and says it deals with desires/passions or bodily appetites. Give part marks for a vague or half-stated idea, such as naming the soul but not Plato, or saying 'desires' loosely. Give no marks for wrong theories or unrelated answers; each point is marked separately.
